## C++17 `earstrip` Polygon Triangulation (`add_polygons` / `addPolygons`)

A GPU only fills triangles. While web mapping libraries typically triangulate polygons on the browser's single-threaded JavaScript main thread, `glmap` triangulates polygons in **C++17** using [`GLMap/earstrip`](https://github.com/GLMap/earstrip) (`src/earstrip.h`) paired with a zero-copy R `SEXP` ring adapter:

- **Zero Per-Ring Heap Allocations**: Reads `sf`'s column-major `N x 2` `REALSXP` matrices directly in C++ without copying vertices into intermediate `std::vector` containers.
- **Branchless 64-Bit Dent Bitmask & 1D Buckets**: Packs and triangulates **50,000 polygons (350,000 vertices $\rightarrow$ 200,000 triangles) in 20 milliseconds**.
- **Hybrid Constrained Delaunay (CDT) Fallback**: Automatically resolves self-intersecting bowtie/figure-8 rings and polygons with `> 128` interior holes.

## Choropleths: Idiomatic `glmap` vs. Drop-In `leaflet`

### 1. Idiomatic `glmap` Choropleth (No Palette Function Boilerplate)
Pass `fill_color = ~column` and `palette = "YlOrRd"` (or `"viridis"`, `"plasma"`, `"magma"`, `"turbo"`, `"RdYlBu"`). `glmap` computes a 256-entry RGB lookup table and attaches a legend automatically:

```{r}
library(glmap)
library(sf)

nc <- sf::st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf"), quiet = TRUE)

glmap(nc, basemap = "positron") |>
  add_polygons(
    fill_color = ~BIR74,
    palette = "YlOrRd",
    fill_opacity = 0.75,
    line_color = "#ffffff",
    line_width = 1.5,
    highlightOptions = highlight_options(weight = 3, color = "#0f172a", bringToFront = TRUE),
    popup = gl_popup_table(nc, zcol = c("NAME", "BIR74", "SID74"))
  )
```

### 2. Binned / Quantile / Categorical Choropleths (`color_bin`, `color_quantile`, `color_factor`)
When you want explicit interval bins (`color_bin()` / `colorBin()`) or equal-count quantiles (`color_quantile()` / `colorQuantile()`)—exact parity with the [Posit Leaflet Choropleth Tutorial](https://rstudio.github.io/leaflet/articles/choropleths.html):

```{r}
bins <- c(0, 1000, 2000, 3500, 5000, 8000, 15000, Inf)
pal <- color_bin("YlOrRd", domain = nc$BIR74, bins = bins)

labels <- sprintf(
  "<strong>%s County</strong><br/>%s births",
  nc$NAME, format(nc$BIR74, big.mark = ",")
) |> lapply(htmltools::HTML)

glmap(nc, basemap = "positron") |>
  add_polygons(
    fill_color = ~pal(BIR74),
    line_color = "#ffffff",
    line_width = 1.5,
    fill_opacity = 0.75,
    highlightOptions = highlight_options(weight = 4, color = "#0f172a", bringToFront = TRUE),
    label = labels
  ) |>
  add_legend(
    position = "bottomright",
    pal = pal,
    values = ~BIR74,
    title = "Births (1974)"
  )
```

## Unfilled Outlines, Polylines, Geodesic Circles & Rectangles

### Polylines (`add_lines` / `addPolylines`) & Unfilled Polygon Rings (`fill = FALSE`)
Pass `sf` lines, `maps::map()` objects, or a `data.frame` / 2-column matrix (such as a `chull()` convex hull):

```{r}
quakes_sub <- head(datasets::quakes, 100)
hull <- quakes_sub[grDevices::chull(quakes_sub$long, quakes_sub$lat), ]

glmap(quakes_sub, basemap = "dark") |>
  add_polygons(data = hull, lng = ~long, lat = ~lat, fill = FALSE, color = "#facc15", weight = 2.5) |>
  add_points(~long, ~lat, color = ~mag, palette = "plasma", radius = 5)
```

### Geodesic Circles (`add_circles` / `addCircles`) vs. Pixel Markers (`add_points`)
- **`add_points()` / `addCircleMarkers()`**: `radius` is measured in **screen pixels** (stays constant size as you zoom).
- **`add_circles()` / `addCircles()`**: `radius` is measured in **meters on the ground** (scales with the map as you zoom in/out):

```{r}
cities <- data.frame(
  city = c("Montreal", "Quebec City", "Ottawa"),
  lon = c(-73.5673, -71.2080, -75.6972),
  lat = c(45.5017, 46.8139, 45.4215),
  pop = c(1762949, 549459, 1017449)
)

glmap(cities, basemap = "positron") |>
  add_circles(
    lon = ~lon, lat = ~lat,
    radius = ~sqrt(pop) * 18,
    fill_color = "#0284c7",
    fill_opacity = 0.35,
    popup = ~paste0("<b>", city, "</b>: ", format(pop, big.mark = ","))
  ) |>
  add_rectangles(
    lng1 = -76.0, lat1 = 45.1,
    lng2 = -70.8, lat2 = 47.1,
    fill = FALSE,
    color = "#ef4444",
    weight = 2
  )
```
